title: Greenville, a hilltop seat on William Campbell's land
summary: Muhlenberg County was formed in 1798, and in 1799 Col. William Campbell gave 30 acres of high ground with two springs for its seat. Greenville got a log courthouse in 1800, a charter in 1812, the railroad in 1871, and then coal.
bodyMarkdown:
Greenville began with a gift of land on a hill. When the legislature carved Muhlenberg County out of Logan and Christian counties at the end of 1798, the new county had settlers and a name but no town.

## A county without a seat

The county was [formed in 1798 and named for Gen. Peter Muhlenberg](https://grokipedia.com/page/Muhlenberg_County,_Kentucky), a minister who had led a Virginia regiment of German settlers in the Revolution. Some of his old soldiers had settled there. The nearest thing to a town was Caney Station, a small fort that Col. [William Campbell](/people/#william-campbell-muhlenberg) and a few associates, enslaved people among them, had raised around 1795.

The first county court met on May 28, 1799, in the home of John Dennis, a tavern keeper. Dennis offered land for a courthouse. So did Campbell, and the justices chose his.

## Campbell's gift

That spring Campbell [donated 30 acres on high ground](https://grokipedia.com/page/Greenville,_Kentucky), with two springs and a crossing of pioneer trails. Alney McLean, the county's first surveyor, laid out a grid of 50 lots around a public square, and the plan was recorded on September 23, 1800. By that fall a log courthouse stood on the square, and a log jail followed. James Weir and James Craig had opened the first store in 1799, and in 1801 Samuel Russell became the first postmaster.

The name is usually traced to Gen. [Nathanael Greene](https://grokipedia.com/page/Nathanael_Greene), another Revolutionary War hero. Local tradition credits Campbell's wife, Tabitha, often called the "Mother of Greenville," who is said to have had the green treetops around the hill in mind as well. The Campbells also gave the land for the [Presbyterian church, established in 1804](https://history.ky.gov/markers/first-presbyterian-church-1821).

## A slow start

Growth came slowly. Greenville had 26 people in 1800 and about 75 in 1810. The General Assembly formally established the town on January 6, 1812, but it was not incorporated as a city until 1848. Farmers around it raised wheat, corn and tobacco, and by 1840 the Martin family was turning tobacco into plug on North Main Street.

The circuit rider [Peter Cartwright](/people/#peter-cartwright) came with Philip Kennerly to [form new Methodist churches](https://history.ky.gov/markers/greenville-methodist-church) in the county, and Greenville's congregation dates from 1820.

Greenville also had its war heroes. Ephraim M. Brank, who came from North Carolina around 1808, was remembered for his [cool daring on the breastworks at New Orleans](https://history.ky.gov/markers/muhlenberg-hero) on January 8, 1815. In the Civil War, Confederate cavalry under Nathan Bedford Forrest rode through three times.

## Rails and coal

By 1870 the town had 557 people. The railroad arrived in 1871, and by 1873 the population had roughly doubled, to about 1,000. Coal did the rest. Kentucky's [first commercial coal mine](/stories/mclean-drift-bank-kentuckys-first-commercial-coal-mine/) had opened in Muhlenberg County in 1820, and after the Civil War the county became one of the state's great coal producers.

It led Kentucky in underground production from 1908 to 1913, when its mines were already producing more than 2 million tons a year.

## Kentucky today

The square Alney McLean laid out is still the center of town. The [Neo-Classical courthouse built in 1907](https://grokipedia.com/page/Greenville,_Kentucky) stands on it, and the county's state historical marker is on the lawn, where the map pin sits.
